payload.title: Silescelida
payload.wikitext:
{{Short description|Genus of extinct archosauriform}} {{Speciesbox | fossil_range = [[Middle Triassic]], {{fossilrange|Ladinian|Ladinian|[[Ladinian]]}} | image = Silescelida skeletal.png | image_caption = Skeletal reconstruction showing known remains | display_parents = 3 | genus = Silescelida | parent_authority = Garcia et al., [[2026 in reptile paleontology|2026]] | species = acristata | authority = Garcia et al., 2026 }} '''''Silescelida''''' is an [[extinct]] genus of [[eucrocopoda]]n [[archosauriform]] known from the [[Middle Triassic]] ([[Ladinian]] age) [[Santa Maria Supersequence]] of Brazil. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Silescelida acristata''''', known from a fragmentary skeleton. [[Phylogenetic analyses]] suggest affinities of ''Silescelida'' with the [[Euparkeriidae]], which is otherwise unknown from South America. == Discovery and naming == {{Location map|Brazil | width = 225px | float = left | relief = yes | coordinates={{coord|29|37|38.9|S|53|22|06.5|W|display=inline}} | caption= ''S. acristata'' [[Type locality (biology)|type locality]] in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil | pushpin_relief=1 }} The ''Silescelida'' fossil material was discovered in the Posto site of the [[Pinheiros-Chiniquá Sequence]] of the [[Santa Maria Supersequence]] ([[Paraná Basin]]). These outcrops are located within [[Quarta Colônia State Park]] in [[Dona Francisca]] municipality of [[Rio Grande do Sul]], Brazil, and are assigned to the ''[[Dinodontosaurus]]'' [[Assemblage Zone]]. The specimen is housed in the [[PUCRS Museum of Science and Technology|Museum of Science and Technology]] at the [[Pontifical Catholic University of Rio Grande do Sul]] (PUCRS), where it is permanently [[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] as specimen MCP 4186-PV. It consists of a left [[Scapula#In other animals|scapula]], right [[Ilium (bone)#Other animals|ilium]], and left [[Femur#Other animals|femur]], found in association. Based on their comparable size, they likely all came from the same individual. At some point following its discovery, the [[Anatomical terms of location#Proximal and distal|proximal]] end of the femur, on which the collection code for the specimen had been inscribed, was lost. As a result, the data associated with its provenance was inaccessible until it was rediscovered in 2022, more than 20 years later. In 2026, Maurício S. Garcia and colleagues [[Species description|described]] ''Silescelida acristata'' as a new genus and species of early-diverging eucrocopodan archosauriform based on these fossil remains, establishing MCP 4186-PV as the [[holotype]] specimen. The [[Genus|generic name]], ''Silescelida'', combines the [[Latin]] word {{lang|la|siles}}, meaning {{gloss|silence}} with the [[Greek language|Greek]] word {{lang|grc|skelēs}}, meaning {{gloss|hind leg}}, alluding to the loss of that part of the holotype and its long-unknown provenance. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''acristata'', combines the Latin prefix ''a-'', meaning {{gloss|without}}, with the Latin {{lang|la|cristāta}}, meaning {{gloss|crested}}. This references the distinctive lack of a protuberance on the femur for the attachment of the [[caudofemoralis]] muscle. == Classification == [[File:Euparkeria white background.png|thumb|[[Life restoration]] of the similar ''Euparkeria'']] To test the affinities and relationships of ''Silescelida'', Garcia et al. (2026) included it in an updated version of the [[phylogenetic]] matrix of Sengupta et al. (2024). The resolution of their results varied based on which taxa were included, with some versions producing large, unresolved [[polytomies]]. Their best-resolved results, which restricted character scorings to the holotype of the Polish ''[[Osmolskina]]'' (rather than including additional referred material) and combined the Chinese ''[[Halazhaisuchus]]'' with "''[[Turfanosuchus]]''" ''shageduensis'' as a single operational taxonomic unit (OTU), are displayed in the [[cladogram]] below. ''Silescelida'' was recovered in a clade including the ''Halazhaisuchus'' and the German ''[[Marcianosuchus]]'', which all exhibit anatomical traits comparable to the South African ''[[Euparkeria]]'', which was recovered in the next-diverging clade alongside the Chinese ''[[Wangisuchus tzeyii]]'', together forming the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Euparkeriidae]]. This would make ''Silescelida'' the first early-diverging eucrocopodan found in the Triassic of Brazil, all other archosauromorphs from this region falling into the more [[Basal (phylogenetics)|derived]] clade comprising [[Proterochampsia]] and [[Archosauria]]. It is also the first euparkeriid-like taxon found in South America. {{clade |{{clade |1={{extinct}}''[[Tasmaniosaurus triassicus]]'' |2={{clade |1={{extinct}}''[[Osmolskina czatkowicensis]]'' |2=[[National Museum, Bloemfontein|NMQR]] 3570 }} |label3=[[Archosauriformes]] |3={{clade |1={{extinct}}[[Proterosuchidae]] |2={{clade |1={{extinct}}[[Erythrosuchidae]] |label2=[[Eucrocopoda]] |2={{clade |1={{extinct}}''[[Cuyosuchus huenei]]'' |2={{clade |1={{extinct}}''[[Asperoris mnyama]]'' |2={{extinct}}''[[Dorosuchus neoetus]]'' |3={{clade |1={{clade |1={{extinct}}''[[Halazhaisuchus qiaoensis]]''
